text: vignette illustrates main use slicer package means toy example. Empirical distributions generated bivariate Gaussian mixtures four isotropic components laid symmetrically around origin. distributions differ one another rotated counterclockwise angle ω∈[0,π/2)\omega \[0, \pi/2). goal analysis retrieve specific angles distributions rotated.

title: (Sliced) Wasserstein kernels and Gaussian process regression
text: Let’s load slicer. generate input distributions, define generate_data(): plots show two empirical distributions, using rotation angle ω=π/16\omega = \pi/16 using one ω=3π/8\omega = 3\pi/8.
code: library(slicer) generate_data <- function(n = 200, a = 5, angle = 0, Sigma = diag(1, 2)) {   mus <- cbind(c(a, 0), c(0, a), c(-a, 0), c(0, -a))   R <- rbind(     c(cos(angle), -sin(angle)),     c(sin(angle), cos(angle))   )   cluster <- sample(1:4, size = n, replace = TRUE)   d <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = 2)   for (i in 1:4) {     d[which(cluster == i), ] <- MASS::mvrnorm(       sum(cluster == i), mu = mus[, i], Sigma = Sigma     )   }   d %*% t(R) } set.seed(20261127)  op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE, bty = "n") par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) generate_data(angle = pi/16) |>    plot(xlab = "first dimension", ylab = "second dimension", asp = 1) generate_data(angle = 3*pi/8) |>    plot(xlab = "first dimension", ylab = "second dimension", asp = 1) par(op)

title: (Sliced) Wasserstein kernels and Gaussian process regression

code: sample_size <- 200 N_train <- 40 N_test  <- 20 angle_range <- c(0, pi/4)  angles <- runif(N_train + N_test, angle_range[1], angle_range[2])  distributions <- vector("list", N_train + N_test) for (i in seq_len(N_train + N_test)) {   distributions[[i]] <- generate_data(angle = angles[i]) }

code: M1 <- matrix(rnorm(50), ncol = 5) M2 <- matrix(rnorm(50), ncol = 5) M3 <- matrix(rnorm(250), ncol = 5)  # Sliced Wasserstein of order 2 my_directions <- generate_directions(20, 5) compute_all_distances(list(M1, M2, M3), my_directions,   average = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) #>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3] #> [1,] 0.0000000 0.6104348 0.4788046 #> [2,] 0.6104348 0.0000000 0.5193320 #> [3,] 0.4788046 0.5193320 0.0000000  # Sliced Wasserstein of order 1 compute_all_distances(list(M1, M2, M3), my_directions, p = 1,   average = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) #>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3] #> [1,] 0.0000000 0.4833153 0.3750074 #> [2,] 0.4833153 0.0000000 0.4101071 #> [3,] 0.3750074 0.4101071 0.0000000  # Marginal squared 2-Wasserstein distances: marginal_wass <- compute_all_distances(list(M1, M2, M3), diag(1, 5),   average = FALSE, verbose = FALSE) marginal_wass[[3]] # along third dimension #>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3] #> [1,] 0.0000000 0.6347678 0.3158111 #> [2,] 0.6347678 0.0000000 0.5919710 #> [3,] 0.3158111 0.5919710 0.0000000  # Reweight projection directions (shear transformation) A <- diag(c(4, 0.5, 3, 2, 1)) shear_wass <- compute_all_distances(list(M1, M2, M3), diag(1, 5), A = A,   average = FALSE, verbose = FALSE) shear_wass[[3]] #>           [,1]     [,2]      [,3] #> [1,] 0.0000000 1.904303 0.9474332 #> [2,] 1.9043034 0.000000 1.7759130 #> [3,] 0.9474332 1.775913 0.0000000

title: Predict Outcomes Using Gaussian Process Regression — gpr_predict
text: Computes posterior mean predictions Gaussian process regression model given precomputed kernel matrices. implementation follows Algorithm 2.1 Rasmussen Williams (2006), optional centring step automatic jitter escalation handle near-singular kernel matrices.

title: Predict Outcomes Using Gaussian Process Regression — gpr_predict
code: gpr_predict(   Kxx,   Kxstar,   y_train,   centre = TRUE,   lambda2 = 1e-06,   Kxstarstar = NULL )

title: Predict Outcomes Using Gaussian Process Regression — gpr_predict
text: Kxx Kernel matrix evaluated training inputs. Kxstar Matrix kernel values test training inputs. row corresponds one test input. y_train Vector training outcomes. centre TRUE (defaults), training outcomes centred around mean. lambda2 Kernel noise variance. Kxstarstar Optional. square matrix kernel values among test inputs. NULL (default), posterior means computed returned vector. Else posterior mean vector covariance matrix returned.

title: Predict Outcomes Using Gaussian Process Regression — gpr_predict
text: Kxstarstar NULL (default), vector posterior mean predictions test inputs. Else, list vector test_predictions posterior mean predictions matrix test_variance posterior covariance test inputs.

title: Predict Outcomes Using Gaussian Process Regression — gpr_predict
code: N1 <- 25 N2 <- 10 x_train <- seq(-pi, pi, length.out = N1) x_test  <- runif(N2, -pi, pi) distance <- outer(c(x_train, x_test), c(x_train, x_test), "-") |> abs() kernel <- rbf(distance, length_scale = 1, variance = 1) Kxx    <- kernel[1:N1, 1:N1] Kxstar <- kernel[(N1+1):(N1+N2), 1:N1] Kxstarstar <- kernel[(N1+1):(N1+N2), (N1+1):(N1+N2)] y_train <- ifelse(x_train == 0, 2*pi, sin(2*pi*x_train) / x_train) curve(sin(2*pi*x)/x, from = -pi, to = pi) points(x_train, y_train) # Only means: don't use Kxstarstar points(x_test, gpr_predict(Kxx, Kxstar, y_train), pch = 16) # Add credible intervals around predictions: gpr_fit <- gpr_predict(Kxx, Kxstar, y_train, Kxstarstar = Kxstarstar) segments(x0 = x_test,          y0 = gpr_fit$test_predictions - 2 * sqrt(diag(gpr_fit$test_variance)),          y1 = gpr_fit$test_predictions + 2 * sqrt(diag(gpr_fit$test_variance)), col = "#4DAF4A")

title: Negative Log Predictive Density for Gaussian Process Regression Models — nlpd_gpr
text: fit Gaussian process model fit obtained gpr_predict() fit_gpr(). y_test vector true test outcomes. add_noise TRUE (default), y_test assumed noisy observation noise added variance posterior covariance. nugget Numeric; base jitter added covariance diagonal needed ensure positive definiteness. Increased multiplicatively required.

title: Negative Log Predictive Density for Gaussian Process Regression Models — nlpd_gpr
text: scalar giving average NLPD. returned value attribute "jitter_used" indicating final diagonal jitter added (0 none).

title: Negative Log Predictive Density for Gaussian Process Regression Models — nlpd_gpr
code: set.seed(2026-06-25) N1 <- 50 N2 <- 20 x_train <- seq(-pi, pi, length.out = N1) x_test  <- runif(N2, -pi, pi) y_train <- x_train * plogis(x_train) * cos(x_train) + rnorm(N1, sd = 0.5) y_test <- x_test * plogis(x_test) * cos(x_test) D2 <- outer(c(x_train, x_test), c(x_train, x_test), "-") |> abs() fit <- fit_gpr(D2, seq_len(N1), N1 + seq_len(N2), y_train, y_test,                runs = 20L, cores = 1) #> Hyperparameter search 1 of 20. #> Optimum set at 65.1049. #> Hyperparameter search 2 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 3 of 20. #> Current optimum improved from 65.1049 to 65.1049. #> Hyperparameter search 4 of 20. #> Current optimum improved from 65.1049 to 65.1049. #> Hyperparameter search 5 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 6 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 7 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 8 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 9 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 10 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 11 of 20. #> Current optimum improved from 65.1049 to 40.4504. #> Hyperparameter search 12 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 13 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 14 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 15 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 16 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 17 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 18 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 19 of 20. #> Hyperparameter search 20 of 20. # noisy outcome nlpd_gpr(fit, y_test + rnorm(N2, sd = 0.5)) #> [1] 1.13033 #> attr(,"jitter_used") #> [1] 0 # clean outcome nlpd_gpr(fit, y_test, add_noise = FALSE) #> Warning: Covariance matrix not positive definite.
